clue.text: In retrospect, not many required to hold down mythical creature

indicators.note: looking back in retrospect tells us to read the whole assembled string from end to start
to hold means the word for not many wraps around the word for down

parts.note: not many means few
to down something, such as a flag, is to lower it

explanation.surface: Looking back, it took only a handful of people to pin down a monster of legend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down' is the verb, as in lowering a flag, not a direction. 'In retrospect' turns the whole thing round once it is built; 'required' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In folklore this is a man who turns into a wolf at full moon, a beast of legend.

clue.text: Euphoria when most important romance is over

indicators.note: most important points to the leading letter, the head of the word for romance
is over means that leading letter is finished with and dropped

parts.note: a relation, as in a love relationship, is a romance

explanation.surface: The thrill fades once the great love affair of one's life has ended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most important' picks the first letter, R, of RELATION, and 'is over' removes it; 'when' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a state of intense happiness and high spirits.

clue.text: Awaiting the extraction of gold from medicine

indicators.note: the extraction of means the letters for gold are pulled out of the word for medicine

parts.note: an expectorant is a cough medicine that loosens phlegm
OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone waits for the precious metal to be refined out of a drug.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking OR out of EXPECTORANT leaves the answer; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To be expectant is to be waiting for something hoped for, such as a birth.

clue.text: Group of people excluded from participation losing heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the phrase for excluded is dropped

parts.note: out of it means left out of the action, excluded

explanation.surface: A team of people left out of the game becomes disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT OF IT has seven letters; 'losing heart' removes the fourth, its central O.
explanation.definitionFit: An outfit is informally a team or organisation of people working together.

clue.text: Hammerhead may go berserk

definitions.meaning: the head of a hammer may work loose and come off its wooden shaft
to go berserk is to lose one's temper wildly

explanation.surface: A hammerhead shark might run amok.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a hammer's head can detach from its shaft; the idiom means suddenly losing one's temper.

clue.text: Being proper's only part of it

indicators.note: part of it means the answer is a run of letters inside the words proper's only

explanation.surface: Correctness is only one piece of the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A being is an individual living creature, as a human is.

clue.text: Worker brought in to clear weed

indicators.note: brought in to means the worker is placed inside the word for clear

parts.note: plain means clear, as in plain to see
an ant is the usual crossword worker, from worker ants

explanation.surface: A labourer is hired to get rid of the weeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantain is a common lawn weed of the genus Plantago, with broad ribbed leaves.

clue.text: Notice in America how different English is

indicators.note: how different signals that the letters of English are made into something else

explanation.surface: A remark on how British usage differs from American.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a comment on transatlantic usage, and that is the joke: in Britain the word means beach pebbles. 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In the US a professional hangs out a small signboard of this name outside an office.

clue.text: Entertainment provided here by things that are black …

parts.note: night is black, as in black as night
clubs are one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Somewhere offers shows put on by dark objects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'things that are black' supplies two pieces, each a dark thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A late-opening venue offering music, dancing and cabaret.

clue.text: What shows the omission without the 'p' in reprimand

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the omission mark goes round the letter

parts.note: a caret is the proofreader's mark showing where something has been left out

explanation.surface: A proofreader explains the mark for a dropped letter p in a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but here it means outside: CARET goes round P. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To haul someone over the coals; the verb comes from being summoned to stand on the boss's rug.

clue.text: Youngster's reign lay in ruins

indicators.note: in ruins means the letters of reign lay are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A child's rule has collapsed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of Youngster's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An animal, especially a racehorse, in its second year, so a young one.

clue.text: Road's principal cause of trouble

parts.note: MI is the M1, Britain's first motorway, the standard crossword road; the possessive adds S
chief means principal, main

explanation.surface: The main cause of trouble is the road.
explanation.walkthrough: MI stands for the M1, the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: Mischief is harm or trouble, or whatever brings it about.

clue.text: Mark and Jack win

parts.note: a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor, and so is a tar
to win something is to get it

explanation.surface: Mark and Jack are victorious.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aimed at, such as a bullseye, is a mark.

clue.text: Sort of snake in the grass

indicators.note: sort of here means a reworked version of the letters in the word snake

explanation.surface: A type of serpent lurking in the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snake in the grass' reads as one phrase, but 'grass' alone is the definition: British slang for an informer. 'in the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a grass is an informer, and a tell-tale who reports others is the schoolyard version.

clue.text: … and here by things that are not

parts.note: snow is white, so not black
white is the opposite of black

explanation.surface: And somewhere offers shows put on by things that are not dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis carries on from 8 down: 'here' means where entertainment is provided, and 'things that are not' means things that are not black.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow White is a fairy tale staged as pantomime and film, a source of family entertainment.

clue.text: What surrounds a flight path? Sky, probably

definitions.text: What surrounds a flight path? Sky, probably

parts.words: What surrounds a flight path? Sky, probably
parts.note: the flight is a flight of stairs, and the shaft it climbs through surrounds its path; 'Sky, probably' is the answer the aircraft reading invites

explanation.surface: A question about what lies around an aircraft's route, with a shrugging guess of sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The vertical shaft in a building that contains a staircase encloses each flight of steps.

clue.text: Ark for two's turned out to be a masterpiece

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of ark for two are turned into a new order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Noah's boat built for pairs ended up a classic.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of two's stands for 'has'; 'to be a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of great creative skill; a masterpiece is the finest example of such a creation.

clue.text: Resent having to ask Barnaby

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Charles Dickens novel

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed at having to make a request of a man called Barnaby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel aggrieved at someone's good fortune, or to give something unwillingly.

clue.text: Not wanting article Margaret's made already

parts.note: off, as in off one's food, means not wanting it
the is the definite article
Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: Margaret has already sewn something nobody wants.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-to-wear clothes are made beforehand in standard sizes, not tailored.

clue.text: Spitfire possibly misusing her gift

indicators.note: misusing means the letters of her gift are put to a wrong use, so rearranged

explanation.surface: A fiery woman is wasting her talent.
explanation.walkthrough: A spitfire is also a hot-tempered woman, which is what the surface pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spitfire was a British warplane of the Second World War, one example of the type.

clue.text: Little bit of vineyard given to doctor

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or its wine, as in grand cru
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A small plot of the vineyard is handed to the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fragment, especially of bread or cake.

clue.text: Coped with old soldier first

indicators.note: first means the soldier comes before the word for old

parts.note: man means an ordinary soldier, as in officers and men
aged means old

explanation.surface: Someone dealt with the veteran trooper before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To have got by or dealt successfully with a difficulty.

clue.text: Tight-fitting hat reveals most of face to a man

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of the word for face is dropped

parts.note: clock is British slang for a face
he is the pronoun standing for a man

explanation.surface: A snug hat shows most of a woman's face to a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clock' is British slang for a face, as in 'clock that'. 'reveals' and 'to' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting bell-shaped woman's hat, fashionable in the 1920s.

clue.text: Conflict about retired English composer

indicators.note: about means the word for conflict goes around the other piece

parts.note: war is armed conflict

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

explanation.surface: A war breaks out over a retired English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses only the English abbreviation, which then sits inside the conflict word under 'about'.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was a German writer of operas such as the Ring cycle.

clue.text: Spheres are versatile

definitions.meaning: spheres are rounded in every direction, read playfully as a description of them
versatile means skilled in many fields

explanation.surface: Globes are adaptable.
explanation.definitionFit: Versatile means good at everything; spheres, whimsically, are every one of them circular.

clue.text: Nurse embraced by one man is betrothed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: embraced by means the word for nurse sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: Ned is a man's name
to tend is to nurse or look after

explanation.surface: A nurse hugged by a single man is engaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One's fiancé or fiancée, the person one is engaged to marry.

clue.text: Bearing the burden

definitions.meaning: in heraldry a bearing is a device shown on a shield
a burden is a load or responsibility laid on someone

explanation.surface: Carrying the load.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry any figure borne on a shield has this name; it is also a duty entrusted to someone.

clue.text: Incense upsets for instance a composer

indicators.note: upsets is read as turning the whole string over, so the two pieces run end to start

parts.note: eg abbreviates exempli gratia, for instance
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: Burning joss sticks bothers a musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Incense' looks like a noun but is the verb, stressed on the second syllable. 'upsets' reads EGARNE backwards; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To incense someone is to make them furious.

clue.text: Still level, we hear, when night falls

parts.note: even means still, as in even better

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word for level is swapped for one sounding the same

parts.note: tied means level, as with scores

explanation.surface: Scores still level, we are told, as darkness comes.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for evening, the time of dusk.
